terms: Ek codebase, ek process, ek deploy.
ms0-what-monolith.analogy: Monolith ek bada joint-family ghar hai: ek rasoi, ek meter, ek darwaza. Simple chalta hai, par ek kamra renovate karna ho to poora ghar disturb hota hai.
ms0-what-monolith.what: Definition: Saari functionality (login, orders, payments, emails) ek hi application mein, ek hi process mein deploy hoti hai. Modules aapas mein function calls se baat karte hain.
ms0-what-monolith.why: Zyadatar products ke liye sabse sahi starting point — simple, fast development, easy debugging.
gotchas: Monolith ≠ bad design — modular monolith bhi hota hai
Performance aksar microservices se behtar (no network hops)

terms: Ek deploy, andar clear module boundaries.
ms0-why-monolith.what: Definition: Monolith har dimension mein simple hai: network calls ki jagah function calls, ek hi debugger, ek hi deploy, easy refactoring aur transactions.
ms0-why-monolith.why: Distributed systems ki complexity tab hi lo jab fayda cost se zyada ho.
ms0-why-monolith.code:
src/
  orders/     (public API: orders/index.ts)
  billing/
  users/
// rule: modules sirf dusre module ka public API import karein (lint rule)
where: Shopify jaisi badi companies bhi modular monolith.
gotchas: Shared DB tables direct access mat
Ye split karne ka rasta bhi saaf rakhta hai

terms: Sirf hot module ko scale karna.
ms0-pain-points.what: Definition: Scale par monolith ke 4 pain points: (1) independent scaling nahi, (2) ek bug sab giraye, (3) deploys slow aur risky, (4) bade teams mein merge conflicts aur ownership unclear.
ms0-pain-points.why: Microservices tabhi justify hote hain jab ye problems real ho rahe hon.
ms0-pain-points.code:
Symptoms:
- build+test 40 min
- release 1x/week kyunki risk
- search ko 10x CPU chahiye par poora app scale
- 5 teams ek hi repo mein bhidte hain
cons: Pain hone se pehle split = over-engineering
gotchas: Pain organizational bhi hota hai, sirf technical nahi

terms: Alag deploy bina baaki ko chhue.
ms0-what-microservice.what: Definition: Microservice chhota, independent process hai jo ek business capability own karta hai — apna code, apna data, apna deploy. Dusre services se network (HTTP/gRPC/events) par baat karta hai.
ms0-what-microservice.why: Teams autonomous ho jaati hain aur services independently scale aur deploy hoti hain.
ms0-what-microservice.code:
orders-service  -> orders DB   (REST + events)
payments-service -> payments DB
inventory-service -> inventory DB
// orders payments ka DB nahi chhoota — sirf API/events
gotchas: Size (lines) nahi, boundary matter karti hai
Network fail hota hai — har call par plan

terms: Microservices ki cost, monolith ki coupling.
K8s, tracing, discovery, CI per service.
ms0-when-not.what: Definition: Chhoti team, unclear domain, early product, ya strong ops skills ke bina microservices mat lo. Galat boundaries ko baad mein badalna monolith se zyada mahanga hota hai.
ms0-when-not.why: Bahut teams microservices apna ke slow ho jaati hain.
ms0-when-not.code:
Checklist: split karne se pehle
[ ] 3+ teams jo block ho rahi hain?
[ ] Domain boundaries stable?
[ ] CI/CD, monitoring, tracing ready?
[ ] Data ownership clear?
(koi 'No' → modular monolith)
gotchas: Team size 5-10 ho to shaayad zaroorat nahi
Pehle ek service extract karke seekho

terms: System org ke communication structure ko mirror karta hai.
ms0-conways-law.what: Definition: 'Jo organization system design karti hai, wo aisa design banati hai jo uske communication structure ki copy ho.' Teen teams = teen modules.
ms0-conways-law.why: Service boundaries team boundaries ke saath align honi chahiye warna constant cross-team coordination.
gotchas: Reverse Conway: target architecture ke hisaab se teams banao
Shared services ownerless ho jaati hain

terms: Ek ka change dusre ko na tode.
msf1.what: Definition: Application chhoti independent services ka collection, har ek business capability par focused, apna data aur lifecycle, lightweight communication.
msf1.why: Scale, resilience, aur team autonomy — par network, consistency aur ops ki cost.
msf1.code:
Characteristics:
- Independent deploy
- Decentralized data
- Smart endpoints, dumb pipes
- Design for failure
- Automated infra (CI/CD, observability)

terms: DDD ka boundary jahan model consistent.
msf2.what: Definition: Services ko business capability ya bounded context se decompose karo, technical layers se nahi. Existing monolith ke liye Strangler Fig: naye features nayi service mein, purane dheere migrate.
msf2.why: Galat decomposition = chatty services aur distributed transactions.
msf2.code:
Galat: ui-service, logic-service, db-service (layers)
Sahi: orders, catalog, payments, shipping (capabilities)
Strangler: API gateway /orders/* -> naya service, baaki monolith

msf3.what: Definition: Sync simple par caller callee ke availability par depend karta hai. Async decouple karta hai par eventual consistency aur complexity laata hai. Mix: queries sync, workflows async.
msf3.why: Resilience aur latency design ka core decision.
gotchas: Sync chains availability multiply karti hain (0.99^n)

terms: Single entry, routing, auth, rate limit.
msf4.what: Definition: Gateway clients ko services ke internal structure se bachata hai. BFF web/mobile ke liye alag tailored APIs deta hai.
msf4.why: Cross-cutting concerns ek jagah aur chatty client calls kam.
msf4.code:
Mobile -> mobile-bff -> orders, users
Web    -> web-bff    -> orders, catalog
Gateway: auth, rate-limit, TLS, routing
gotchas: Gateway mein business logic mat daalo
BFF team client team own kare

msf5.what: Definition: Instances dynamically aate-jaate hain, IPs badalte hain. Discovery: Kubernetes DNS/Services, Consul, Eureka. Health checks se unhealthy remove.
msf5.why: Hardcoded IPs cloud mein kaam nahi karte.

terms: Har service ka private data store.
Dusri service ka DB direct nahi.
msd1.what: Definition: Service ka data sirf uski API se access hota hai. Isse schema changes independent hote hain. Cross-service queries API composition ya CQRS views se.
msd1.why: Shared DB coupling banata hai — schema change sab services todta hai.
msd1.code:
orders-service -> Postgres(orders)
catalog-service -> Elasticsearch
session-service -> Redis
// report chahiye? events se read-model banao, dusre ka DB join mat karo
gotchas: Alag schema same DB server mein bhi coupling kam karta hai par true isolation nahi

msd2.what: Definition: Distributed transaction ki jagah har service local transaction karti hai; fail hone par compensating actions (refund, release stock) chalte hain.
msd2.why: 2PC microservices mein scale/availability ke liye practical nahi.
gotchas: Compensation fail ho sakta hai — retry/alert
Isolation nahi — intermediate state dikhta hai

msd3.what: Definition: CQRS commands (writes) aur queries (reads) alag models mein. Event sourcing state ki jagah events store karta hai — poora history, replay possible.
msd3.why: Read-heavy views, audit trail, aur cross-service queries ke liye.
msd3.code:
Command: PlaceOrder -> events: OrderPlaced, ItemAdded
Projection: OrdersByUser(read DB) <- consume events
state(order) = fold(events)

msd4.what: Definition: Services facts emit karti hain (OrderPlaced); interested services subscribe karti hain. Producer ko consumers ka pata nahi — loose coupling.
msd4.why: Naye consumers add karna producer change kiye bina.
gotchas: Outbox pattern DB write + publish atomic karne ke liye

msd5.what: Definition: Services ke beech strong consistency nahi; eventual consistency accept karo. Tools: sagas, outbox, idempotency keys, reconciliation jobs.
gotchas: Dual-write problem (DB + broker) outbox se solve

msc1.what: Definition: Sync request-response simple hai. REST public/compatible; gRPC internal low-latency. Resilience: timeout, retry, circuit breaker.
msc1.why: Queries aur user-facing flows ke liye natural.

msc2.what: Definition: Producer broker ko message deta hai, consumer baad mein process karta hai. Temporal decoupling, buffering, retry, fan-out.
msc2.why: Spikes absorb karna aur services ko independent rakhna.

msc3.what: Definition: Services ke beech data format agreement. Schema registry compatibility enforce karti hai taaki producer change consumers ko na tode. JSON flexible par untyped.
msc3.why: Independent deploys ke liye safe schema evolution zaroori.

msc4.what: Definition: Ek operation kai services span kare to 2PC (strong consistency, coordinator SPOF, lock holding) ya Saga/TCC (eventual). Microservices mein saga prefer hota hai.
msc4.code:
2PC: coordinator -> prepare(all) -> commit(all)  // participant down = blocked
Saga: local commit + compensation
gotchas: Compensations business-level hoti hain, rollback nahi

terms: @key se services ke beech shared type.
msc5.what: Definition: Federation mein har service apna subgraph own karti hai; router unhe ek unified graph mein jodta hai. Clients ek query se multiple services ka data lete hain.
msc5.why: Frontend ko ek API, backend ko team autonomy.

terms: Kuch trial calls se recovery check.
msr1.what: Definition: Circuit breaker failures count karta hai; threshold cross hone par OPEN — calls turant fail (ya fallback). Timeout ke baad HALF-OPEN mein test requests; success par CLOSED.
msr1.why: Failing dependency par threads/requests waste hona (cascading failure) rokta hai aur use recover hone ka time deta hai.

msr2.what: Definition: Transient failures par retry (exponential backoff + jitter, max attempts). Sirf idempotent operations retry karo. Retry budget rakho.
msr2.why: Bina jitter ke sab clients ek saath retry karke recovering service ko phir giraate hain.
gotchas: POST bina idempotency key retry mat karo

terms: Ek slow dependency baaki ko na khaye.
msr3.what: Definition: Ship ke compartments ki tarah — har dependency ka alag pool/semaphore. Slow service sirf apna pool bharegi, poora app nahi.
msr3.why: Ek slow dependency saare threads le leti hai to sab features girte hain.
gotchas: Pool sizes data se tay karo

msr4.what: Definition: Per-client limits service ko overload se bachate hain. Algorithms: token bucket, sliding window. Gateway ya service level par; distributed ho to Redis.
msr4.code:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
// token bucket: 100 tokens, refill 10/s per API key
cons: Legit bursts block ho sakte hain
gotchas: Load shedding internal services par bhi

msr5.what: Definition: Recommendation service down ho to popular items dikhao, error nahi. Critical vs non-critical features classify karo.
msr5.why: Partial service poori outage se behtar hai.

mst1.what: Definition: Har request ko trace ID milta hai jo services ke beech propagate hota hai (W3C traceparent). Backends: Jaeger, Tempo; instrumentation: OpenTelemetry.
mst1.why: Latency bottleneck kaun si service hai — traces batate hain.
gotchas: Context async boundaries (queues) mein bhi propagate

mst2.what: Definition: Har service stdout par JSON logs likhe; agent unhe central system mein bheje. Fields: timestamp, level, service, traceId, userId (no PII/secrets).
mst2.why: Dozens of services ke logs alag-alag dekhna impractical hai.
mst2.code:
logger.info({ msg: 'order placed', orderId, traceId, durationMs });
// {"level":"info","service":"orders","traceId":"abc","msg":"order placed"}

mst3.what: Definition: Services ke liye RED, resources ke liye USE. Prometheus + Grafana. SLO-based alerts (burn rate) symptom par, cause par nahi.

mst4.what: Definition: Consumer apni expectations (request/response) contract mein likhta hai; provider CI mein verify karta hai. Breaking change deploy se pehle pakda jaata hai — full E2E ki jagah.
mst4.why: E2E tests slow aur flaky; contracts fast aur precise.
gotchas: Sirf jo consumer use kare wohi assert karo

mst5.what: Definition: Service ko real dependencies (DB, Kafka) ke saath test karo — mocks se behtar confidence. Testcontainers har test run ke liye disposable containers deta hai.
mst5.why: Mocks real behaviour (constraints, transactions) miss karte hain.
gotchas: Tests parallel run mein DB share na ho

mso1.what: Definition: Har service ki apni independent pipeline: build → test → image → deploy. Monorepo mein path-based triggers; polyrepo mein shared libs versioning.
mso1.code:
on:
  push:
    paths: ['services/orders/**']
jobs:
  orders:
    steps: [test, build image, push, deploy (argocd sync)]

mso2.what: Definition: Kubernetes containers schedule, scale, heal aur service discovery handle karta hai. Rolling updates, resource limits, probes.
mso2.why: Dozens of services manually manage karna impossible hai.
mso2.code:
readinessProbe, livenessProbe
HPA (CPU/RPS)
PodDisruptionBudget: minAvailable 2
resources.requests/limits

mso3.what: Definition: Blue/Green fast rollback par double capacity. Canary real traffic ke chhote hisse par metrics dekh kar rollout. Mesh/ingress traffic split.
mso3.code:
VirtualService: v1 95% / v2 5%
Analysis: error rate < 1% and p99 < 400ms -> promote
else auto rollback

mso4.what: Definition: Config code se alag (env-specific), secrets encrypted store se, rotation, per-environment values. Feature flags runtime behaviour ke liye.
mso4.why: Same image har environment mein; secrets leak nahi.

terms: Team size, deploy frequency, scale needs.
why-microservices.what: Definition: Microservices tab jab team size, independent scaling ya release cadence demand kare. Martin Fowler: 'MonolithFirst'. Split data-driven ho, trend-driven nahi.
why-microservices.why: Interview mein trade-offs articulate karna sabse zaroori hai.
why-microservices.code:
Split signals:
- 3+ teams ek codebase mein block
- ek module ko 10x scale
- deploy risk high, frequency low
- stable domain boundaries

ddd-intro.what: Definition: DDD business domain ko model karta hai. Aggregate (Order + OrderLines) ek transaction boundary; dusre aggregates IDs se reference. Context map contexts ke relationship batata hai.
gotchas: Ek context ek model — 'Customer' sab jagah alag

kafka-patterns.what: Definition: Kafka distributed append-only log. Key se partition → same key ka order guaranteed. Consumer group scale-out. Exactly-once (idempotent producer + transactions) limited scope mein.

service-mesh.what: Definition: Mesh cross-cutting concerns (mTLS, retries, observability, traffic shifting) application code se nikal ke proxies mein daalta hai. Istio/Linkerd.
service-mesh.code:
PeerAuthentication: STRICT mTLS
VirtualService: retries 3, timeout 2s, canary 90/10
DestinationRule: outlierDetection (ejection)

chaos-engineering.what: Definition: Production-like environment mein failures inject karke resilience verify. Latency, pod kill, dependency down, AZ failure. GameDays teams ko practice dete hain.
chaos-engineering.code:
Experiment: payments latency +2s
Hypothesis: checkout p99 < 3s, circuit breaker opens
Abort: error rate > 5%
Result -> fix timeout config
gotchas: Findings ko backlog mein fix karo

event-storming.what: Definition: Workshop jahan dev + domain experts wall par events timeline banate hain. Phir commands, aggregates, policies, hotspots; clusters bounded contexts suggest karte hain.
event-storming.why: Service boundaries business samajh se nikalte hain, guess se nahi.
event-storming.code:
Timeline (orange events):
CartCheckedOut -> PaymentRequested -> PaymentSucceeded -> OrderConfirmed -> ShipmentScheduled
Hotspots (pink): refund rules unclear
